title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 Where a party, within the time limit prescribed by Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law, applies for retrial to the People's Court at the next higher level of the original trial People's Court on the grounds of the causes for retrial listed in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court at the next higher level shall accept the application according to law.
Article 2 The provisions on suspension, interruption, and extension shall not apply to the time limit for applying for retrial as prescribed by Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 4 Where a party applies for retrial, it shall submit to the People's Court the judgment, ruling, or mediation document that has become legally effective, identity certification, and relevant evidentiary materials.

Article 5 Where the written application for retrial or other materials submitted by the applicant for retrial do not conform to the provisions of Articles 3 and 4 of this Interpretation, or contain personal attacks or other content that may intensify conflicts, the People's Court shall require the applicant for retrial to supplement or correct them.

Article 6 The People's Court shall, within five days after receiving the qualified written application for retrial and other materials, complete the acceptance registration procedures such as sending the notice of acceptance to the applicant for retrial, and send the notice of acceptance and a copy of the written application for retrial to the opposing party.
Article 7 After accepting an application for retrial, the People's Court shall form a collegiate bench to conduct the review.
Article 8 The People's Court's review of an application for retrial shall focus on whether the cause for retrial is established.

Article 9 The "principal evidence needed for trial of the case" as prescribed by Item (5) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law refers to evidence necessary for the People's Court to determine the basic facts of the case.

Article 10 Where the determination of the basic facts and the nature of the case in the original judgment or ruling was made on the basis of other legal documents, and such other legal documents have been revoked or altered, the People's Court may deem it as the circumstance provided for in Item (12) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 11 Where the People's Court, after examining the written application for retrial and other materials, considers that the cause for applying for retrial is established, it shall directly rule for retrial.
Where a party applies for retrial beyond the time limit prescribed by Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law, or beyond the scope of the causes for retrial listed in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall rule to reject the application for retrial.

Article 12 Where the People's Court considers that it is difficult to make a ruling by reviewing only the written application for retrial and other materials, it shall retrieve and review the original trial case file.

Article 13 The People's Court may decide whether to question the parties based on the needs of the case.
Where an application for retrial is made on the ground that there is new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment or ruling, the People's Court shall question the parties.

Article 14 Where, during the review of an application for retrial, the opposing party also applies for retrial, the People's Court shall list it as an applicant for retrial and review its application for retrial together.

Article 15 Where an applicant for retrial applies to withdraw the application for retrial during the case review period, whether to permit it shall be determined by the People's Court by ruling.
Where an applicant for retrial, after being summoned by subpoena, refuses without justifiable reasons to accept questioning, the People's Court may rule to treat the application for retrial as withdrawn.

Article 16 Where the People's Court, after review, considers that the cause for retrial is not established, it shall rule to reject the application for retrial.
The ruling rejecting the application for retrial shall become legally effective upon service.

Article 17 Where, during the period when the People's Court is reviewing the application for retrial, the People's Procuratorate files a protest against the case, the People's Court shall rule for retrial in accordance with Article 211 of the Civil Procedure Law. The specific retrial requests raised by the applicant for retrial shall be included in the scope of trial.

Article 18 Where the People's Court at the next higher level, after review, considers that the cause for retrial is established, it shall generally bring the case up for trial by itself. The Supreme People's Court or a Higher People's Court may also designate another People's Court at the same level as the original trial People's Court to conduct the retrial, or instruct the original trial People's Court to conduct the retrial.

Article 19 The People's Court at the next higher level may decide whether to designate a retrial based on the degree of influence of the case and the circumstances of the participants in the case. Where designation of a retrial is necessary, consideration shall be given to factors such as facilitating the parties' exercise of litigation rights and facilitating the People's Court's trial.
The People's Court that accepts the designated retrial shall conduct the trial in accordance with the procedures provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 207 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 21 Where, in a case in which no party has applied for retrial and no People's Procuratorate has filed a protest, the People's Court discovers that the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement has circumstances such as harming national interests or public interests and indeed has errors, it shall initiate a retrial in accordance with Article 198 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 22 The People's Court shall, in accordance with Article 207 of the Civil Procedure Law, try retrial cases according to the first-instance procedure or the second-instance procedure.
The People's Court shall hold a hearing in trying a retrial case, except where, in a case tried according to the second-instance procedure, both parties have fully expressed their opinions by other means and have agreed in writing not to hold a hearing.

Article 23 Where an applicant for retrial withdraws the application for retrial during the retrial period, whether to permit it shall be determined by the People's Court by ruling. If the ruling permits the withdrawal, the retrial procedure shall be terminated. Where an applicant for retrial, after being summoned by subpoena, fails to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or leaves the court without permission of the court midway, the People's Court may rule to treat the application for retrial as automatically withdrawn.
In a retrial case protested by the People's Procuratorate, where the party who applied for the protest has the circumstances prescribed in the preceding paragraph, and the national interests, public interests, or the interests of a third party are not harmed, the People's Court shall rule to terminate the retrial procedure; where the People's Procuratorate withdraws the protest, it shall be permitted.
Where the retrial procedure is terminated, enforcement of the original judgment shall be resumed.

Article 24 Where, in a retrial case tried according to the first-instance procedure, the first-instance plaintiff applies to withdraw the prosecution, whether to permit it shall be determined by the People's Court by ruling. If the ruling permits the withdrawal, the People's Court shall simultaneously rule to revoke the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document.

Article 25 Where parties reach an agreement through mediation during retrial proceedings, the People's Court shall make a mediation document. The mediation document shall have legal effect after it is signed for receipt by all parties, and the original judgment or ruling shall be deemed to be revoked.

Article 26 Where the People's Court, after retrial, considers that the facts found in the original judgment or ruling are clear and the application of law is correct, it shall affirm the original judgment or ruling; where the original judgment or ruling has defects in fact-finding, application of law, or reasoning, but the adjudicative result is correct, the People's Court shall affirm the original judgment or ruling after correcting the above defects in the retrial judgment or ruling.

Article 27 Where the People's Court, trying a retrial case according to the second-instance procedure, finds that the original judgment has errors in fact-finding or unclear fact-finding, it shall alter the judgment after ascertaining the facts. However, where it is convenient for the original trial People's Court to ascertain the facts and resolve the disputes, the People's Court may rule to revoke the original judgment and remand the case for retrial; where the original trial procedure omitted a party that must participate in the proceedings and no mediation agreement can be reached, or there are other violations of statutory procedures that make it inappropriate to directly make substantive disposition in the retrial procedure, the People's Court shall rule to revoke the original judgment and remand the case for retrial.

Article 28 Where, after a ruling for retrial of a case concluded by mediation, it is found upon trial that the cause raised by the applicant for retrial that the mediation violated the principle of voluntariness is not established, and the content of the mediation agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of law, the People's Court shall rule to reject the application for retrial and resume enforcement of the original mediation document.

Article 29 The parties in a civil retrial case shall be the parties in the original trial case. Where a party in the original trial case dies or terminates, the successor of its rights and obligations may apply for retrial and participate in the retrial proceedings.

Article 30 Where previous judicial interpretations issued by this Court are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail. Matters not provided for in this Interpretation shall be handled in accordance with the previous provisions.
